papers.title: Symmetric List Objects
papers.abstract: Cons-lists are fundamental to functional programming, and are well-understood as initial algebras, and as a concrete construction of free monoids. In category theory, such list objects can be axiomatised internal to any monoidal category, with nil and cons maps, and a recursion mechanism. When strengthened to support parametrised recursion, they can be shown to give the free monoid construction. We study a small variant on parametrised list objects called parametrised symmetric list objects, in a symmetric monoidal category, where the two frontmost elements are allowed to be permuted. We show that this gives a construction of free commutative monoids, and develop some related theory.

papers.title: Partial Markov Categories
papers.abstract: We introduce partial Markov categories as a synthetic framework for synthetic probabilistic inference, blending the work of Cho and Jacobs, Fritz, and Golubtsov on Markov categories with the work of Cockett and Lack on cartesian restriction categories. We describe observations, Bayes' theorem, normalisation, and both Pearl's and Jeffrey's updates in purely categorical terms.

papers.title: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of deriving transformations
papers.abstract: A differential category is an additive symmetric monoidal category with an algebra modality, axiomatizing smooth functions, and a deriving transformation, axiomatizing the differentiation of these smooth functions. An algebra modality may or may not have both the nullary and the binary Seely isomorphisms. Lemay proved that if an algebra modality has both Seely isomorphisms, then it has at most one deriving transformation. It was then an open problem whether every algebra modality has at most one deriving transformation. We answer this question in the negative by constructing algebra modalities with infinite sets of deriving transformations. We also clarify the relations between the nullary Seely isomorphism, the binary Seely isomorphism, and uniqueness of deriving transformations (that is, the property for an algebra modality to have at most one deriving transformation). First, we refine Lemay's theorem by removing the assumption of the nullary Seely isomorphism. Then, we show by means of various examples that the six combinations of absence or presence of nullary Seely isomorphism, binary Seely isomorphism, and uniqueness of deriving transformations, which are not already ruled out by the refined uniqueness theorem, can be realized.

papers.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
papers.abstract: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

papers.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism. We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints. On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal. The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].

papers.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
papers.abstract: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions. Moreover, we give two applications. First, we show that the additive equivalence discovered by Cummings and Gratz between the Paquette-Yildirim completion and a specific metric completion of an Igusa-Todorov discrete cluster category is, in fact, a triangulated equivalence. Second, we fully classify metric completions of bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves over weighted projective lines of domestic or tubular type.

papers.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
papers.abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.

papers.title: Monoidal structures on triangulated fibered categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a small category admitting binary products. There exists a canonical dictionary expressing the structure and properties of monoidal $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories in terms of the external tensor product in place of the usual internal tensor product. In this paper, we specialize this dictionary to the setting of triangulated $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories, by studying how the general translation process interacts with shift functors. Our results provide a satisfactory abstract framework to study monoidal structures from the perspective of perverse sheaves.

papers.title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
papers.abstract: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with more than one constant or in duals of elementary toposes.

papers.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
papers.abstract: There are many types of equivalence relations in mathematics, each one enjoying its own defnition, but many of them can also be defined by transformations of morphisms: Green's relations, orbit relations, conjugacy, equality of orbit closures, equivalence of Cauchy sequences, stable isomorphism. We unify them through the comparison category of a comparison datum, read at levels $-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (comparisons in both directions, connected components, homotopy groups). Its normal form is a full subcategory of a Grothendieck construction $\int_VH$ cut out by a map $s$; the classical relations are traced back to it by restriction along $s$, enrichment by a cost (limit relations) and filtered colimits (stabilization). If the map $\sigma$ transporting morphisms into a $2$-category is arbitrary, every relation occurs, so the constraint is the regularity of $\sigma$. We grade data along seven regularity classes. The rigid and diagonal classes are classified completely (on finite groups, by the double coset relations); completely functorial data contain conjugacy and obey a dichotomy on nil monoids. Whether every relation on a monoid is level $0$ of a completely functorial datum is open.

papers.title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
papers.abstract: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $\omega$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.

papers.title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
papers.abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.

papers.title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
papers.abstract: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrow\Omega\Sigma X$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

papers.title: Graftings and cograftings for species
papers.abstract: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Non-linear contexts and dependent operads
papers.abstract: We study the category $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$ of finite posets and opfibrations between them, and prove that it is a perfect operator category in the sense of Barwick. Based on its additional properties, we propose a definition for a dependent operator category, and formulate a notion of dependent affine operad in a fibered way. In the particular case of $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$, we investigate the basic theory of such operads, establishing that the category of algebras for an operad is monadic over a canonical presheaf topos of "dependent sets". We finally extend this theory to a setting where we allow variable duplication, which we refer to as general dependent operads.

papers.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
papers.abstract: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

papers.title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
papers.abstract: Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

papers.title: Affinizations and braided module categories
papers.abstract: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.

papers.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

papers.title: Process matrices on generalised theories
papers.abstract: We extend the process-matrix framework for defining indefinite causal orders to a broad class of generalised physical theories. We give a simple re-axiomatisation of spacetime contexts in terms of naturality over classical probes, which precisely captures non-contextual assignment together with compatibility with convexity and coarse-graining within local laboratories. Using this compositional perspective, we give a clean characterisation of theories in which abstract spacetime contexts admit a process-matrix representation, and we pin down the precise conditions (satisfied by classical theory, quantum theory, and a Boxworld-like theory) under which the supermap and process-matrix perspectives on higher-order processes coincide.

papers.title: Categorification in Representation Theory
papers.abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the relatively young subject of $2$-representation theory, which studies categorifications of important players in classical representation theory. In particular, we provide a streamlined exposition of the main results leading to the classification of simple $2$-representations for Soergel bimodules associated to finite Weyl groups in characteristic $0$, obtained in [M. Mackaay, V. Mazorchuk, V. Miemietz, D. Tubbenhauer and X. Zhang, Simple transitive $2$-representations of Soergel bimodules for finite Coxeter types. Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023)].

papers.title: Dynamical systems as enriched functors
papers.abstract: This article presents a general description of dynamical systems using the language of enriched functors and enriched natural transformations. This framework is essential to establish the equivalence of three descriptions of dynamics -- a semigroup action on the domain; a parameterized family of endomorphisms; and a transformation of time-space into the collection of endomorphisms. A collection of categorical axioms are presented that provides a complete categorical language to develop dynamical systems theory. None of the assumptions are rooted in specific contexts such as topology and measure spaces. The equivalence of the three descriptions is further used to construct other related notions,such as transfer operators, orbits and shift-spaces. All of these objects are defined by their structural role and universal properties, instead of their usual pointwise definitions.

papers.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
papers.abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.

papers.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result. Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

papers.title: Hyperstructures as complete atomic Boolean algebras
papers.abstract: We show that several categories of hyperstructures, including the mosaics of Nakamura and Reyes and the hypergroups of Marty, are realizable as categories of objects with extra structure within the category of complete atomic Boolean algebras (CABAs) and atom-preserving morphisms.
